title: Element distinctness: Theta(N) classical queries vs Theta(N^(2/3)) quantum queries (Ambainis quantum walk)
problem_statement: Given oracle access to x_1, ..., x_N (values from a set of size M >= N), decide whether all N values are distinct, and if not, find i != j with x_i = x_j.

input.size_measure: Query model: cost is the number of oracle calls (each returns one x_i).

algorithms.name: classical: read everything, sort, scan
algorithms.idea: Query all N values, sort them, and compare neighbours.
algorithms.pseudocode: read x_1..x_N; sort; report an equal adjacent pair if any
algorithms.time_complexity: N queries; O(N log N) comparisons

algorithms.name: Ambainis quantum walk algorithm
algorithms.idea: A quantum walk over sets of r = N^(2/3) indices whose queried values are kept in a register; a set is marked if it contains a colliding pair, and a walk step exchanges one index, which costs O(1) queries.
algorithms.time_complexity: O(N^(2/3)) queries, bounded error (running time is also analysed in the paper; not recorded here)
algorithms.space_complexity: O(N^(2/3)) values held in quantum registers
algorithms.correctness: Ambainis 2007 (arXiv quant-ph/0311001): 'For element distinctness ... we get an O(N^(2/3)) query quantum algorithm', improving an O(N^(3/4)) algorithm of Buhrman et al. and matching the lower bound of Shi (as stated in the arXiv abstract).

lower_bounds.source: Elementary reduction from the OR function on N - 1 bits (randomized query complexity Theta(N)): set x_0 = 0 and x_i = i if y_i = 0, x_i = 0 if y_i = 1; the values are all distinct iff OR(y) = 0, and each query of x costs at most one query of y.

lower_bounds.bound: Omega(N^(2/3)) queries for bounded error (Ambainis's algorithm is optimal up to a constant factor)
lower_bounds.source: Aaronson & Shi 2004 (from the collision lower bound; Shi's abstract: 'implies a quantum lower bound of Omega(n^(2/3)) queries ... for the element distinctness problem'); Ambainis 2005 extends it to small ranges (all M >= N)

relationship: POLYNOMIAL separation in the query model, established in the literature and tight on both sides by the cited bounds (Ambainis 2007; Aaronson & Shi 2004; Ambainis 2005; cited, not checked here; the classical lower bound is only sketched in lower_bounds): Theta(N) classical queries (even randomized) vs Theta(N^(2/3)) quantum queries. Element distinctness is harder than the collision problem quantumly (N^(2/3) vs N^(1/3)); informally, it has no 2-to-1 promise: there may be a single colliding pair. The quantum-walk technique that achieves it became a general tool (the abstract notes the generalisation to finding k equal items with O(N^(k/(k+1))) queries).

sources.title: Quantum Walk Algorithm for Element Distinctness
sources.note: arXiv preprint quant-ph/0311001 (first version November 2003); the query bounds quoted in this entry were checked against its abstract.

sources.title: Quantum lower bounds for the collision and the element distinctness problems
Polynomial Degree and Lower Bounds in Quantum Complexity: Collision and Element Distinctness with Small Range
sources.note: Crossref holds no title for this DOI; title, volume and pages confirmed on theoryofcomputing.org (2026-10-06).

verification.method: Cited from the literature. DOIs, titles, years, volumes, issues and pages checked against Crossref (and theoryofcomputing.org for the 2005 paper); the query bounds checked against the arXiv abstracts of Ambainis (quant-ph/0311001) and Shi (quant-ph/0112086), and the Theory of Computing abstract of Ambainis 2005. Not implemented: a quantum-walk simulation on lib/qsim.py would need a register of N^(2/3) values and is left open (see research/2026-10-07_quantum_entries.md).

caveats: A separation relative to an oracle, and only polynomial; it does not imply BQP != BPP. The classical lower bound counts queries; in the comparison model, classical TIME is Theta(N log N). The quantum algorithm has bounded error. The quantum lower bound of Aaronson & Shi was first proven for large ranges; the small-range case (M close to N) is due to Ambainis 2005.
notes: Pairs naturally with pairs/collision-problem-classical-vs-quantum: the same lower-bound technique (polynomial method) gives N^(1/3) for collision and N^(2/3) for element distinctness. The classical TIME side of the same problem (all pairs, Theta(N^2), vs sorting, O(N log N)) is recorded separately in pairs/element-distinctness-pairs-vs-sorting (added in parallel on 2026-10-06); this entry concerns query complexity.
